units.text: 10. Gaps, risks and open questions
Risk
Why it matters
What would show it, or reduce it
One vendor sets the economics
Free public minutes, free governance and the ref semantics are GitHub's to change; the Actions terms limit use to the repository's own software project
GitHub's pricing and terms pages; a self-hosted runner as the fallback
The subscription token in CI

Anthropic documents it but advises an API key for a shared secret, its terms assume ordinary, individual usage, its rules for subscriptions moved several times in 2026, and bare mode will stop reading the token
Questions R6; keeping an API-key path in the workflows
One plan's window for every Actions worker
All workers share one person's five-hour and weekly limits; this project's own account reached its weekly limit on 2026-10-15 with several threads running
The planned cap of 10 Claude runs a day; one plan per worker
Symphony's own tests run private for now

Its plan runs the owner's first fresh test on private repositories only until the Phase 3 rails exist (the run cap, the qa check, checks pinned to Actions), though it recommends public repositories for the code workers change where possible; so Symphony's own runs have not yet tested the free-minutes story
Phase 3 landing
GitHub's rate limits before minutes
GITHUB_TOKEN gets 1,000 requests an hour per repository and the library has no retry on 429 or secondary limits yet
The measurement pass (question R3)
Maturity
The library is days old, 0.4.1 is the last release, later fixes are unreleased, and no full-scale benchmark of Symphony exists
Question R1; the next release
The name
openai/symphony (about 27,700 stars, Apache-2.0) also claims issues for coding agents
Question R10
Beethoven's evidence is mostly plans
Only splits.py of the research gates exists; the symbolic gate is a bounded search for most conditions, not a proof
Question R8
Beethoven's setting
Wayne State requires approval of AI tools; a personal plan has no BAA; Remote Control is unavailable under the HIPAA configuration and stores transcripts on Anthropic's servers
Written answers from the university and Anthropic, already preconditions of any paid edition
Prompt injection through issues
Claude workers in Actions read issue text and hold write tokens
Recorded decisions: only writers queue work, code owners guard the files that steer workers
The public story is untold
The site and READMEs never mention Actions, free minutes or cost; several internal documents lag GitHub's current behavior
The manual's talking points; a pass over the docs
The server enforces a claim only at its creation

Git refuses a second creation of claude/N, but GitHub accepts a fast-forward or forced push onto an existing claim under the recommended setup, since rulesets must leave claude/** alone. Only the local push guard refuses forced pushes, and on 2026-10-15 it was found to read the session's own directory rather than the clone a git -C command names, so a lease onto another worker's claim passed when run from a directory whose clone had neither branch, though it was refused from either worker's own clone
research/taxonomy/verify/02; a fix to the guard; question R4
The idle clock is the pusher's

Idleness is read from the head commit's committer date, which the pusher writes: a commit dated in the future holds a claim indefinitely, against the coordinator and a person's release alike, and one dated in the past is released at once. This is finding F8, open in 0.4.1 and on main
The unmerged F8 fix reads GitHub's record of the push, falling back to the commit date when that record is missing; question R4
A reopened issue can be orphaned
The labels claimed and in-review stay on a closed issue; if it is reopened, the board lists it nowhere and no worker is dealt it until a person takes them off
A board rule for reopened issues; question R4
Open questions that are not risks:
Whether a public, Claude-free Beethoven gate library is wanted, which is the only way Beethoven gets free minutes.
Which subset of the taxonomy's twelve axes a short public explanation should use (the manual proposes three).
Whether the experiment, once complete, belongs in this spec; it stays out of the grant until you say so.
11. Research questions
Each question owns the Open claims named in it. A question is answered only when its acceptance criteria are met; until then the claim keeps its grade.
Question
Answered when
R1
Does Symphony's protocol beat one agent, and the other two-agent arms, at a matched budget?

The coordbench full run you chose on 2026-10-15 (35 new pairs under five arms, plus the runs to redo) reports pass rates with exact tests and confidence intervals, and tokens, wall time and list-price dollars per pair; any gap under the roughly 15-point noise floor is reported as not established
R2
Is the combination in section 8 unique?

A documented search (FSE, ICSE and ASE 2026, arXiv cs.SE and cs.MA, GitHub topics, the awesome lists of agent orchestrators) scores every candidate on the five mechanisms of section 8; claim U1 stands only if none has four of the five, or (a), (c) and (d) together
R3
What does one coordination step cost, and which GitHub limit binds first?

The canary measures API calls per board run, the medians from claim to first pull request and from open to merge, and the number of concurrent workers at which GITHUB_TOKEN's 1,000 requests an hour or the 100-run queue gives out; the library retries on 429 and secondary limits
R4
Does the claim hold on github.com as it does on a local git server?

The canary records a second creation of claude/N, a push that descends from another worker's claim, a forced push with and without a ruleset, the rename on release, and a push after a merge; the clock question of F8 is settled
R5
Are Actions workers, benchmarks and a paid App inside GitHub's Actions terms?

GitHub's written answer, or a lawyer's reading, on three cases: Claude workers writing the repository's own code; coordbench running other projects' tasks; SymphonyBoard's open runtime running in customers' Actions
R6
Can several Actions workers run on one person's subscription token, and will that keep working?

Anthropic's written answer on a token in an organization secret, several parallel workers on one plan as ordinary, individual usage, and claude-code-action under bare mode; and a tested fallback that uses an API key
R7
What are free public minutes worth to an adopter?

For three workloads (one maintainer, a small team, a research lab), the monthly minutes and their price on a private repository, and the same work's price on gh-aw with an API key and on Copilot's agents in credits, with every assumption stated and every price linked
R8
Do Beethoven's checklist gates catch what reviewers miss?

REFORMS and CLAIM gates built for the first study catch seeded faults of the kinds Luo et al. found (leakage, post-hoc selection, metric misuse) that a reading of the paper alone misses; and a search names any other system that gates these checklists in code, or finds none
R9
Does the taxonomy separate the field?

Every system in section 5 is placed on all twelve axes with sources, no two systems practitioners treat as different share all twelve cells, and a systematic search confirms or refutes that no published taxonomy has a compute-payer axis
How much does the name cost?
The first page of results on the main search engines and registries for Symphony with agents, coding or Claude is captured, with a recommendation: keep it, qualify it, or rename
The manual's section on deep research turns these into one message to paste.
